headline: Join the British Army Reserve in 2026
metaDescription: Join the British Army Reserve in 2026: age limits, fitness standards, minimum 19 or 27 days a year, daily pay from £63.27, tax-free bounty and how to apply.

sections.content:
Army Reservists serve part-time alongside a civilian job, training in the evenings, at weekends and on an annual camp. They take part in everything the Regular Army does, from combat roles and humanitarian work to specialist support, and they can deploy on operations when their unit is called upon.

Most Reservists join a regional unit near home, while some join national units that recruit across the country for specialist roles. The Army states that family life and civilian jobs come first, so training is designed to fit around work and personal commitments.
sections.title: What Army Reservists Do

sections.content:
You can apply from 17 years and nine months old so you are ready to join on your 18th birthday. Soldiers must enlist before their 43rd birthday, while officers must apply by 48 years and nine months and start training by their 50th birthday. Rejoiners may join as soldiers until 52 and as officers until 57.

Applicants must pass a basic fitness assessment. Reserve infantry standards include a 50kg mid-thigh pull, a medicine ball throw of at least 2.7 metres and a 2km run in 10 minutes and 15 seconds. Medical, background and nationality checks also apply.

sections.content:
Reservists are paid for every day they train, on the same pay scale as a Regular soldier of the same rank and role. Entry-level Reserve soldiers earn from £63.27 a day during initial training, rising to around £95.06 a day as a corporal and £106.73 a day as a sergeant.

Depending on the unit, the minimum commitment is 19 or 27 days a year, rewarded with a tax-free annual bounty that grows with years of service. Reservists also receive subsidised food and travel while on duty, a pension, and an HM Forces Railcard costing £15 with a 34% rail discount.
